newsitem.title: CHINA: China ends subversion trial of labour activists.
newsitem.headline: China ends subversion trial of labour activists.

text.p: The trial of two Chinese labour activists on the capital charge of subversion ended on Monday, but the court withheld sentencing on the eve of a visit by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher.

The Intermediate People's Court in the southern city of Shenzhen wrapped up the trial of Li Wenming, 28, a former journalist, and Guo Baosheng, 24, a philosophy student at People's University, for conspiring to subvert the government, court officials said.
The court had postponed proceedings twice last week after the trial of the little known activists attracted the attention of foreign media.
They were detained in May 1994 for trying to form a labour union, the Hong Kong-based Information Centre of Human Rights and Democratic Movement in China said.
The court withheld its verdict on Monday because Christopher was due to arrive in Beijing on Tuesday for a three-day visit, the human rights group said.
Asked to comment on the accusation, prosecutor Liu Hanjun told Reuters: "It is more normal for a court not to deliver its verdict as soon as a trial ends."

But Liu, speaking in a telephone interview from Shenzhen, declined to comment on why a Beijing court sentenced dissident and former student leader Wang Dan to 11 years in prison shortly after his trial ended.
Court officials declined to say when the verdict on the labour activists would be announced.
The two defendants, who pleaded not guilty, face a minimum of 10 years in prison and a maximum penalty of death if convicted.
There has been no precedent in China of an acquittal of a defendant charged with conspiring to subvert the government, the human rights group said.

A former law student involved in the establishment of the labour union has been ordered to serve three years at a labour camp, the group said, adding that a worker has been sent to a labour camp to serve one year.
The whereabouts of six others involved in forming the union are unknown, it said.
